text:
Matt Coronato opened the season as a power-play regular and a points player: 16 in 24 games, 7 with the man advantage. The last ten have been a different story. Two points, both goals, where our numbers would expect about 7.6 at his ice time.

It's a mix, and it isn't all bad luck. Calgary is getting fewer chances with him on the ice (8.9 expected goals over that stretch against 11.1 usual), and the ones he does get aren't going in. His shooting is 9.8% for the season, below his likely range. The odd part: his ice time is up 1:32 a night, so the Flames are leaning on him more, not less, through the slump.

The skill hasn't left. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 98th percentile last season in scoring chances from the home-plate area and 93rd percentile in primary shot assists. The issue is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents generating 0.33 more expected goals per 60 with him out there last season, bottom 1% of forwards, and his 5v5 numbers this year still trail his team's. What to watch: whether the chances come back before the minutes go.
headline: Coronato's quiet November, and why it's mixed
